documents.unit: AI at UC (AI Enablement Community of Practice)
documents.title: Guidelines on AI use
documents.stance_why: The page sets no default rule and sends students to instructors and syllabi: "Check with faculty members" and "Review course syllabi". It calls itself "a compass" and not "a list of restrictions", so the decision is delegated.
documents.summary: General UC guidance with sections for general use, students and research. It stresses UC-licensed tools, public data only, and checking instructors and syllabi before using AI. It sets no course-level AI stance.

units.why: The opening line frames the guidance as "a compass" and not "a list of restrictions", which sets the document's purpose and principles; this is an institution-level framework, so P56, not a rule.
units.anchor: not intended as a list of restrictions, but as a compass
units.frag_end: ethical and practical landscape of AI

units.why: "We champion academic integrity, discovery, and human-centered responsibility" states the principles behind UC's AI approach, an institutional principles statement (P56) rather than a rule.
units.anchor: We champion academic integrity, discovery, and human-centered responsibility

units.why: "As this field evolves, so will our approach" says the guidance is provisional and invites participation ("ongoing conversation"), matching P54.
units.anchor: As this field evolves, so will our approach

units.why: "Log into UC tools with your UC credentials" directs users to university-licensed AI tools; institution-wide, so P92 and not the course-tool type P17.
units.anchor: Log into UC tools with your UC credentials

units.why: The text says licensing agreements give "privacy-protected access to approved AI and Generative AI tools"; it names vetted tools as the privacy-protecting choice, so P50.
units.anchor: privacy-protected access to approved AI and Generative AI tools

units.why: "Neither controlled nor restricted data are approved for use in AI tools" bans classes of data from AI tools; a data-protection rule, P50.
units.anchor: Neither controlled nor restricted data are approved for use in AI tools

units.why: The instruction to "Verify that the data you intend to interact with is classified" as Public before using AI is a pre-use data check, P50.
units.anchor: Verify that the data you intend to interact with is classified
units.frag_end: before using AI or Generative AI tools
units.policy: Verify that the data intended for use with AI or Generative AI tools is classified as Public under the Data Classification Policy before using those tools.

units.why: "UC student directory data is not approved for use in AI tools" bans a specific data class from AI tools; a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: UC student directory data is not approved for use in AI tools

units.why: "exercise caution to avoid inadvertently sharing personal information" is advice on protecting personal data, P50.
units.anchor: exercise caution to avoid inadvertently sharing personal information

units.why: "complies with legal requirements, copyright laws, and ethical standards" ties AI use to existing law; P77 rather than P52 because it is a general compliance duty, not a rule about ownership of output.
units.anchor: complies with legal requirements, copyright laws, and ethical standards

units.why: Students are told to "Communicate with your instructors about the acceptability and appropriate use" of AI before using it; this is ask-the-instructor guidance, P10.
units.anchor: Communicate with your instructors about the acceptability and appropriate use

units.why: Faculty "can provide clear guidance about how these tools may or may not fit into their learning objectives"; the university leaves acceptability to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: how these tools may or may not fit into their learning objectives
units.fit_note: Also ties the decision to the course learning objectives and evaluation criteria (P83).

units.why: "Carefully read the syllabi for each of your courses" makes students responsible for finding each course's AI rules, P78.
units.anchor: Carefully read the syllabi for each of your courses

units.why: "or reach out to your instructor if you're unsure" tells students to ask when the syllabus is unclear, P10.
units.anchor: reach out to your instructor if you're unsure

units.why: "should align with the UC Student Code of Conduct" binds student AI use to the existing code; P77 (existing university policy), since it does not say AI misuse is misconduct outright.
units.anchor: should align with the UC Student Code of Conduct

units.why: "Investigators are encouraged to indicate ... the extent to which ... generative AI technology was used" is a disclosure request for research proposals; P62 (research use).
units.anchor: Investigators are encouraged to indicate in the project description
units.fit_note: Also a disclosure-of-AI-use request, but for research proposals, not student submissions.

units.why: NSF and NIH reviewers are told to "pay attention" to notices, one of which prohibits generative AI in NIH peer review; this defers to funder rules, which P62 covers.
units.anchor: If you serve as an NSF or NIH reviewer, please pay attention

documents.title: AI Applicable Policies
documents.stance_why: The page sets no stance on whether AI may be used. It lists existing policies that apply to AI (e.g. "The Acceptable Use policy is applicable to the use of AI"), so it carries other rules over and neither allows nor bans AI.
documents.summary: A list of existing UC policies (data governance, acceptable use, accessibility, security review, conduct, export control) stated to apply to AI use. It adds no AI-specific teaching rules.

units.why: The page says it "ensures AI enablement across the institution aligns with the university's broader data governance and information security standards", a statement of scope and purpose, P56.
units.anchor: ensures AI enablement across the institution aligns with the university's broader data governance

units.why: "are required to comply with these policies while utilizing AI" makes existing security policies binding for AI use, P77.
units.anchor: are required to comply with these policies while utilizing AI

units.why: "The Data Governance and Classification Policy is applicable when using AI" extends an existing data policy to AI, P77.
units.anchor: The Data Governance and Classification Policy is applicable when using AI

units.why: "The Acceptable Use policy is applicable to the use of AI" extends the acceptable-use policy to AI, P77.
units.anchor: The Acceptable Use policy is applicable to the use of AI
units.frag_end: applicable to the use of AI

units.why: The EIT Accessibility Policy sets standards for "design, development, acquisition and use of electronic and information technology resources, including AI", so P97.
units.anchor: design, development, acquisition and use of electronic and information technology resources, including AI

units.why: Security Review requires risk assessments for IT solutions "including AI"; this is institutional review of AI tools, P65.
units.anchor: Information security risk assessments
units.policy: Information security risk assessments (Information Security Reviews) are necessary to identify and document information security risk related to new or existing university information systems or IT solutions, including AI, and provide recommendations to mitigate the identified risk.

units.why: "Students and employees ... are required to comply with these policies while utilizing AI" makes conduct rules binding on AI use, P77.
units.anchor: are required to comply with these policies while utilizing AI

units.why: "The Student Code of Conduct is applicable to the use of AI" ties student AI use to the code and its sanctions; P77 rather than P36 because it does not itself call any AI use misconduct.
units.anchor: The Student Code of Conduct is applicable to the use of AI
units.frag_start: The Student Code of Conduct is

units.why: "The use of AI must comply with Export Control Regulations" for students is a legal compliance rule, P77.
units.anchor: The use of AI must comply with Export Control Regulations

units.why: Employees "may receive disciplinary action, up to and including termination, for conduct and/or rules violations" under the conduct rules that apply to AI use; a consequence under existing policy, P77.
units.anchor: An employee may receive disciplinary action, up to and including termination
units.fit_note: States a sanction (P37-like) but not specific to AI.

units.why: "AI may not be used in a manner that creates a conflict of interest" is a conduct rule on employees' AI use, P77 (existing conflict-of-interest policy).
units.anchor: AI may not be used in a manner that creates a conflict of interest
units.frag_start: collective bargaining agreement or for whom

units.why: "AI may not be used to engage in any form of harassment" is a general ban on malicious AI use, P74.
units.anchor: AI may not be used to engage in any form of harassment

units.why: "The use of AI must comply with Export Regulations" for faculty and staff is the employee version of the export-control compliance rule, P77.
units.anchor: The use of AI must comply with Export
units.frag_start: All faculty, staff, volunteers, and visitors

notes: No school or computing-unit AI policy found; course layer deferred. Neither document states a classroom AI stance.
